articles.title: SOLAR ECLIPSE October 23, 2014
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) hosted a public viewing event for the October 23, 2014, solar eclipse at Hogue Park, attracting a diverse crowd of all ages to observe the phenomenon and a sunspot. The article also serves as a look ahead, encouraging early planning for the highly anticipated total solar eclipse across North America in August 2017.

articles.title: Observer's Handbook 2015
articles.summary: This document begins with an introduction to the Royal Astronomical Society of Canada's 'Observer's Handbook 2015', emphasizing its utility for astronomical data. It then presents two articles: one by Manoj Kaushik advocating for binocular astronomy, highlighting its ease of use and wide field of view for casual sky exploration compared to large telescopes. Separately, Mark McCarthy details his rewarding experience observing the October 8, 2014 total lunar eclipse and various deep-sky objects like Uranus and the Orion Nebula through his Dobsonian telescope under exceptional sky conditions.

articles.title: The Leonids Meteor Shower
articles.summary: The article describes the Leonids Meteor Shower, detailing its peak dates on November 16 and 17, 2014, with optimal dark sky conditions due to a waning crescent moon. It explains that the Leonids originate from debris left by Comet Tempel-Tuttle and are named for their radiant in the constellation Leo. Viewers can expect to see around 20 meteors per hour, with suggestions for best viewing times and directions.

articles.title: All Three NASA Mars Orbiters Healthy After Comet Flyby October 19, 2014
articles.summary: NASA's three Mars orbiters (Mars Odyssey, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, and MAVEN) successfully weathered the close flyby of Comet C/2013 A1 Siding Spring on October 19, 2014, by taking shelter behind Mars. India's Mangalyaan orbiter also repositioned safely during the event. All spacecraft are healthy and were involved in studying the comet and its potential effects on the Martian atmosphere.

articles.title: KID SPOT
articles.summary: This 'Kid Spot' section features astronomy-themed content for children, including jokes and a quiz on topics like the Pleiades and stellar classification. It also provides a 'Night Sky Challenge' for November 2014, highlighting events like the Leonid Meteor Shower, planetary sightings, and the Orion Nebula, alongside a reminder about the end of Daylight Savings Time.

articles.title: Constellations
articles.summary: The article provides details about Pegasus, a northern constellation named after the mythical winged horse. It highlights its inclusion in ancient and modern astronomical catalogs, its brightest stars (Epsilon Pegasi, Alpha, Beta, Gamma), and its neighboring constellations. The constellation's IAU abbreviation is 'Peg', and it hosts the ancient globular cluster M15, discovered in 1746.

articles.title: Club Updates
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers several resources and services, including an astronomy book and DVD library for members, which is looking to expand its children's section. They also host free 'Telescope Fix It' sessions where experts assist community members with telescope repairs and collimation, regardless of weather. Additionally, SJAA coordinates 'School Star Parties,' providing evening observing sessions for schools in mid-Santa Clara County.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announced its 60th anniversary, an upcoming swap meet, and a new chair for the Imaging Group, alongside a call for a new Advanced Loaner Program lead. Board meeting excerpts from October 2014 covered an incident at RCDO, discussions with the City of San Jose regarding facility reuse, financial updates, and renewals for Mendoza Ranch. The article also mentioned a successful solar eclipse event and progress on a beginners' class.
